title: First cotangent homology classes and zero relations descend along directed unions
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $(S_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be a nonempty family of $R$-subalgebras of $S$, directed under inclusion and with union $S$. Thus every pair is contained in a third member and every element of $S$ belongs to some $S_\lambda$. For any commutative $R$-algebra $D$, let $Q_D=R[x_d\mid d\in D]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $I_D$ be the kernel of evaluation $Q_D\to D$, and put $T_1(D/R)=\ker(I_D/I_D^2\to D\otimes_{Q_D}\Omega_{Q_D/R})$, where $\bar f\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm df$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. All maps on $T_1$ are the canonical maps induced by inclusions of algebras and $x_d\mapsto x_d$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Then (i) every $h\in T_1(S/R)$ is the image of an element of $T_1(S_\lambda/R)$ for some $\lambda$; (ii) if $h\in T_1(S_\lambda/R)$ maps to zero in $T_1(S/R)$, there is $\mu$ with $S_\lambda\subseteq S_\mu$ such that $h$ maps to zero in $T_1(S_\mu/R)$.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), constant-base directed inclusions; elementwise consequences for the kernel of the canonical two-term naive cotangent differential.

proof.text: For an $R$-subalgebra $A\subseteq S$, denote by $j_A:Q_A\to Q_S$ the variable inclusion. This map is injective: distinct monomials on the set $A$ remain distinct monomials on $S$, and their coefficients in $R$ are unchanged. Evaluation satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_S j_A=\iota_A\operatorname{ev}_A$, by checking constants and variables, where $\iota_A:A\hookrightarrow S$. Consequently $j_A(f)\in I_S$ if and only if $f\in I_A$, since $\iota_A$ is injective. Every finite collection of polynomials in $Q_S$ uses only finitely many variable labels in $S$, by the finite-monomial definition of the polynomial ring. These labels all belong to one $S_\lambda$: select a member for each label and repeatedly use directedness to find a common upper member. For no labels use nonemptiness. Reinterpret the same monomials over that member to lift all the polynomials. When a specified $S_{\lambda_0}$ must also be contained in the chosen member, take a further common upper member with $S_{\lambda_0}$. This argument requires neither injectivity of $R\to S$ nor finite generation of any subalgebra.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof: $R[S]=\operatorname{colim} R[S_\lambda]$ and $I=\operatorname{colim} I_\lambda$, expanded by finite monomial support.

proof.text:
For any $R$-algebra $D$, apply the arbitrary-variable polynomial differential basis theorem with variable set $D$ and with $Q_D\to D$ the evaluation map. It identifies $D\otimes_{Q_D}\Omega_{Q_D/R}$ with the free $D$-module on $e_d=1\otimes\mathrm dx_d$ and gives
$$1\otimes\mathrm df=\sum_{d\in D}\operatorname{ev}_D(\partial_d f)e_d.$$
Thus a representative $f\in I_D$ defines a class in $T_1(D/R)$ precisely when all the displayed coefficients vanish. Here, explicitly, on a monomial $r\prod_t x_t^{n_t}$ the operator $\partial_d$ produces $n_d r x_d^{n_d-1}\prod_{t\ne d}x_t^{n_t}$ if $n_d>0$, and zero otherwise; extend over finite sums. For an inclusion $A\subseteq S$, this monomial formula gives $j_A(\partial_a f)=\partial_a j_A(f)$ for $a\in A$, while $\partial_s j_A(f)=0$ for $s\notin A$. Evaluating and using step 1 gives $\iota_A(\operatorname{ev}_A(\partial_a f))=\operatorname{ev}_S(\partial_a j_A(f))$. These are actual coefficient identities, so no assertion that a tensor map is injective is needed.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differential basis and partial-derivative calculation; Tag 07BQ, the free differential term of the canonical presentation.

proof.text: Let $h\in T_1(S/R)$. Since $T_1(S/R)$ is a submodule of $I_S/I_S^2$, choose $f\in I_S$ representing its underlying conormal class. By step 1 choose $\lambda$ and $f_\lambda\in Q_{S_\lambda}$ with $j_{S_\lambda}(f_\lambda)=f$. Evaluation and injectivity of $S_\lambda\hookrightarrow S$ imply $f_\lambda\in I_{S_\lambda}$. Since $h$ is in the differential kernel, step 2 says $\operatorname{ev}_S(\partial_s f)=0$ for all $s\in S$. The coefficient identity in step 2 and injectivity of $S_\lambda\hookrightarrow S$ give $\operatorname{ev}_{S_\lambda}(\partial_a f_\lambda)=0$ for every $a\in S_\lambda$. The same basis theorem therefore places $[f_\lambda]$ in $T_1(S_\lambda/R)$. The presentation-functoriality statement sends this class to $[j_{S_\lambda}(f_\lambda)]=[f]$ in the conormal quotient, hence to $h$ in its kernel submodule. This proves (i), with the exact canonical map in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), finite-support descent of a differential-kernel class; Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), induced map on the conormal quotient and its kernel.

proof.text: Let $h\in T_1(S_\lambda/R)$ map to zero, and represent its conormal class by $f_\lambda\in I_{S_\lambda}$. The functoriality statement identifies its image with $[j_{S_\lambda}(f_\lambda)]$, so $f:=j_{S_\lambda}(f_\lambda)\in I_S^2$. By the definition of the product ideal, write $f=\sum_{k=1}^n p_kq_k$ with $p_k,q_k\in I_S$: an additional polynomial coefficient in a generator of the product ideal is absorbed into $p_k$, which remains in $I_S$. Apply the finite-support construction in step 1 to these finitely many factors, also requiring the resulting member $S_\mu$ to contain $S_\lambda$. Let $p_{k,\mu},q_{k,\mu}\in Q_{S_\mu}$ be their lifts. The evaluation identity and injectivity into $S$ imply that every lift is in $I_{S_\mu}$. Let $f_{\lambda,\mu}$ denote the variable inclusion of $f_\lambda$ in $Q_{S_\mu}$. Both $f_{\lambda,\mu}$ and $\sum_k p_{k,\mu}q_{k,\mu}$ map to $f$ under the injective map $j_{S_\mu}$, hence are equal. Therefore $f_{\lambda,\mu}\in I_{S_\mu}^2$. Presentation functoriality identifies the image of $h$ with its class, which is zero in the conormal quotient and thus zero in the kernel submodule. This proves (ii). Empty sums and zero polynomials are covered by the same argument, taking any upper member containing $S_\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof: descent of $I/I^2$, with a finite product-ideal witness written out; Tag 00S1, the representative formula for the induced kernel map.
